subject: Acme POC: access credentials, evaluation plan, and success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Acme POC - access, success criteria, and next steps

Hi Jane — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the POC rolling next week: 

Summary of ask
- Scope: 2-week POC to validate Retriever + generation pipeline for order-tracking use case (search + summarization).
- Primary success criteria (draft attached): 1) >= 85% accurate order retrieval on curated test set; 2) median response latency < 500ms for 95% of queries; 3) acceptable cost per 1k tokens (TBD with your finance).

Access & provisioning needed from your side
1) List of users to invite via SSO (Okta) for both engineering and product reviewers.
2) IP ranges to whitelist for our API key and webhook callbacks.

What Redwood will provide
- SSO invites (SAML Okta) and service account API keys for programmatic runs.
- A POC evaluation plan and sample prompt set (attached).
- 1-hour kickoff + onboarding session: proposed Mon Mar 16, 10:00am PT.

Attachments: acme-poc-success-criteria-template.docx, redwood-poc-access-instructions.txt

Please confirm: 1) the people to invite, 2) the IP ranges to whitelist, and 3) whether you want us to create a long-lived service API key or rotate short-lived keys via your CI. Once we have those, Dev will provision SSO invites and API credentials and share a secure link.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this started.
—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>

Thanks Marissa — this is great. Quick responses: 

1) Users to invite: myself (jane.doe@acme.com), Tom Nguyen (tom.nguyen@acme.com), and backend lead (will share samir@acme.com momentarily).
2) IP ranges to whitelist: 203.0.113.0/24 and 198.51.100.14 (our CI runner).
3) For the service API key, we'd prefer a short-lived key flow integrated with our CI if possible, but we can take a long-lived key for initial testing if that speeds things up.

Can you also confirm whether the evaluation plan includes any synthetic load tests (we want to validate cost under expected concurrency)?

Thanks — we can do the kickoff on Mon Mar 16 at 10am PT.


Jane Doe

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme POC - access, success criteria, and next steps

Thanks Dev — and thanks Jane for the quick replies. Confirming next steps and evaluation plan below (also uploaded to the shared Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/ACME-POC-EVAL-PLAN

POC timeline and ownership\- Week 1 (Mar 16–20): onboarding, baseline dataset runs, initial qualitative feedback (Owners: Acme product + Redwood solutions: Marissa, Dylan)\- Week 2 (Mar 23–27): load testing, cost/perf tuning, final metrics and handoff (Owners: Acme eng + Redwood SRE: Dev)

Success criteria (finalize during kickoff)\- Order retrieval accuracy >= 85% on the provided validation set\- Median response latency < 500ms for 95th percentile at nominal concurrency\- Integration stability: no more than 1 failed webhook delivery per 1,000 requests

Evaluation plan highlights\- Dataset: Acme will provide a labeled validation set (min 500 queries).\- Metrics: precision/recall for retrieval, median & p95 latency, tokens per session & estimated $/1k tokens.\- Artifacts: we will deliver a short evaluation report and suggested config (quantization/batching) to hit your latency/cost targets.

Access confirmation\- SSO invites were sent (check spam if you don't see them).
- API key: you should have a secure link to retrieve the key: https://redwood.app/secure-keys/ACME-POC-0426
- IPs whitelisted as requested.

Kickoff: Mon Mar 16, 10:00am PT — calendar invite sent. Agenda: 1) quick architecture & integration notes, 2) handoff to engineers, 3) confirm data access and validation set, 4) schedule synthetic load window.

Next steps for you before kickoff\- Confirm Samir's email for dev invites.\- Upload validation set to the shared Drive folder.

If you're good with the plan, we'll move forward as scheduled.
\Best,
Marissa
